title: Convolutions, Kernels, & Feature Maps
description: Master sliding kernels, dot products, stride, padding, edge detection filters, and output feature map dimensionality.

slides.title: The Mechanics of a Convolution 🔍
slides.content:
# Sliding Window: The Kernel

A **kernel (or filter)** is a small learnable weight matrix (typically $3 \times 3$ or $5 \times 5$) that slides across an input image.

At each position, it computes the element-wise product with the underlying image patch and sums the results, adding a bias term to produce one scalar pixel in the output **feature map**.

### Output Spatial Dimension Formula:
$$W_{\text{out}} = \left\lfloor \frac{W_{\text{in}} - K + 2P}{S} \right\rfloor + 1$$

* **$K$ (Kernel Size):** Spatial size of the filter matrix.
* **$P$ (Padding):** Zero pixels added around image borders.
* **$S$ (Stride):** Step size the filter shifts per step.

slides.title: Convolution Hyperparameters 🎛️
slides.content:
# Tuning Convolutional Layers

| Hyperparameter | Description | Effect when Increased |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Kernel Size ($K$)** | Width & height of filter matrix (e.g. $3 \times 3$) | Captures wider local context per layer; increases parameters |
| **Stride ($S$)** | Number of pixels the filter shifts per step | Downsamples spatial resolution; reduces computation |
| **Padding ($P$)** | Border pixels appended around boundary | Preserves spatial size; prevents edge pixels from being dropped |
| **Channel Depth ($C$)**| Number of parallel filters applied | Extracts richer, multi-faceted feature abstractions |

quizData.question: If an input image is 28x28 pixels and you apply a 3x3 convolution with stride=1 and padding=1, what is the spatial dimension of the output feature map?
quizData.explanation: Formula: (28 - 3 + 2(1)) / 1 + 1 = 27 / 1 + 1 = 28. 'Same' padding preserves spatial dimensions exactly.

slides.title: Sobel Edge Detection Filter in NumPy 🐍
slides.content: Handcrafted Sobel filter highlighting vertical edges in pixel arrays:
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np

# 3x3 Sobel vertical edge filter
sobel_v = np.array([[-1, 0, 1],
                   [-2, 0, 2],
                   [-1, 0, 1]])

# Sample 5x5 image patch with a sharp vertical transition
patch = np.array([
    [10, 10, 200, 200, 200],
    [10, 10, 200, 200, 200],
    [10, 10, 200, 200, 200],
    [10, 10, 200, 200, 200],
    [10, 10, 200, 200, 200]
])

# Convolve center 3x3 patch with Sobel filter
center_patch = patch[1:4, 0:3]
response = np.sum(center_patch * sobel_v)
print('Vertical edge activation response:', response)

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Stacking 3x3 Kernels 🚀
slides.content:
## Why Modern CNNs Standardize on 3x3 Kernels
VGG demonstrated that stacking two $3 \times 3$ convolutional layers has the identical effective receptive field as a single $5 \times 5$ layer, but uses **28% fewer parameters** and introduces two non-linear activations instead of one!
